All three are list CRDTs that give every character a unique ID and order concurrent inserts deterministically. They differ in what happens when two people type at the same position at the same time.| Algorithm | Interleaves concurrent typing? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RGA | Yes, in some cases | Simple, widely implemented |
| YATA | Rarely, but forward and backward typing can still interleave | Used by Yjs |
| Fugue | No (maximal non-interleaving) | Tree of left and right children |The decisive case is two people typing "hello" and "world" at the same spot: Fugue keeps "helloworld" or "worldhello", never "hweolrllod".Interleaving is not a correctness bug, it is a usability bug. Nobody files a ticket; they just stop trusting the editor.Siblings are ordered by ID, replica first and then counter. That tie-break is part of the spec, so the Rust port must match it exactly. Back to [[CRDT primer]].

A deleted character stays in the tree as a tombstone, because an insert generated concurrently with the delete may name it as a parent. Removing it too early makes that insert impossible to place.When a tombstone can goA tombstone is collectable once every replica that could still reference it has seen the delete. In practice that means a stable version vector: the minimum over all live replicas.Snapshot the note at the stable vectorDrop tombstones whose delete is covered by itRetire replicas that have not synced for 90 days, after a final warningToday the live notes carry about 18 percent tombstones by element count. We are not collecting yet; the plan is in [[Version vectors in practice]].See also [[CRDT primer]] for why deletes are marks, not removals.

The browser holds a WebAssembly build of the CRDT and an IndexedDB copy of every open note. Edits apply locally first; the sync stream sends them when a connection exists.HandshakeClient sends its version vector.Server replies with every operation the client is missing.Client sends its own missing operations.Both sides stream live operations from then on.Revoked access while offlineIf someone loses access while offline, the server refuses their batch when they reconnect. The client keeps the refused text as a local draft so nothing they typed disappears silently.The server is the only place a viewer's edit can be refused: a CRDT merges whatever it is given.Version vector handshakeRejected batch handling in the clientResumable uploads for very large offline sessionsDepends on [[Version vectors in practice]] and [[CRDT primer]].

Proposal: one sequence per note, with a marker element at the start of every block. Pressing Enter inserts a marker; Backspace at the start of a block deletes one. Concurrent typing inside a block always survives a split or merge, because no text is copied.AttributesEach marker carries last-writer-wins attributes: block type, indent level, checked state and code language, ordered by Lamport timestamp and then replica.| Attribute | Example | Conflict rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| type | heading2 | last writer wins |
| indent | 3 | last writer wins |
| checked | true | last writer wins |
| language | rust | last writer wins |Until the wire format has a marker operation, the seed data stores the marker as an ordinary character. Background in [[CRDT primer]] and [[Fugue versus RGA and YATA]].

Numbers from the reference engine on a 2023 laptop. The reference engine walks a linked list for every local edit, so local inserts are linear in note length; the optimised engine will be compared against it operation for operation.| Workload | Ops | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Type 10k characters at the end | 10,000 | 41 ms | append path |
| Type 10k characters at random positions | 10,000 | 2.3 s | linear walk dominates |
| Merge two 5k-op replicas | 10,000 | 18 ms | remote ops are cheap |
| Decode a 100k-op batch | 100,000 | 9 ms | varint decoding |import statistics

def summarize(samples_ms):
    return {
        "p50": statistics.median(samples_ms),
        "p99": sorted(samples_ms)[int(len(samples_ms) * 0.99) - 1],
    }Next step: an order-statistic tree so random-position inserts stop being linear. See [[CRDT primer]].

Raft keeps a replicated log consistent across a cluster by electing one leader per term. The leader accepts writes, appends them to its log and replicates them; an entry is committed once a majority has persisted it.Moving partsLeader election, with randomised timeouts: [[Raft leader election timeouts]]Log replication through AppendEntries, with consistency checks on the previous index and termLog compaction with snapshots: [[Raft log compaction and snapshots]]Membership changes: [[Membership changes with joint consensus]]Reads that stay linearizable: [[Linearizable reads with ReadIndex]]Our metadata cluster runs five voters across three zones, which tolerates the loss of two voters or one zone.Raft is not simpler than Paxos because the problem is simpler. It is simpler because it picks one way to do each thing and explains it.Operational procedures are in [[Raft cluster runbook]].

Changing the voter set in one step can produce two disjoint majorities. Joint consensus avoids that: the cluster first moves to a configuration that needs a majority of the old set and a majority of the new set, then to the new set alone.Add the new node as a learner and let it catch up.Propose the joint configuration.Once committed, propose the new configuration.Remove the old node only after the new configuration commits.Learner supportJoint configuration in the logAutomatic removal of nodes that stay unreachable for a dayNever remove two voters at once from a five-node cluster during an incident. Part of [[Raft overview]]; procedures in [[Raft cluster runbook]].

A leader cannot answer reads from local state blindly: it might have been deposed without knowing. ReadIndex fixes that without writing to the log.Record the current commit index as the read index.Send a round of heartbeats and wait for a majority to answer, which proves leadership.Wait until the state machine has applied up to the read index.Serve the read.Lease reads skip step 2 by trusting clocks for a bounded lease. We do not use them: clock drift on the old hypervisors was measured at up to 400 ms.Part of [[Raft overview]].

We run the consensus layer inside a simulated network that delays, drops, duplicates and reorders messages, driven by a seed so every failure replays.FaultsPartition the leader from a minority, then from a majorityPause a node for longer than the election timeoutRestart a node with its last 100 log entries truncatedSkew one node's clock by two secondsChecks after every stepAt most one leader per termCommitted entries never changeEvery node's applied log is a prefix of the leader'sscenario: leader-isolation
seed: 4242
steps:
  - partition: [n1]
  - wait: 2s
  - heal: all
expect:
  leaders_per_term: 1Background: [[Raft overview]], [[Raft leader election timeouts]].

Procedures for the metadata cluster. Run every command from the bastion; never edit the data directory by hand.Replace a failed nodeConfirm the node is really gone: no heartbeats for ten minutes and the host is unreachable.Start the replacement as a learner with a new node ID.Wait until its match index is within 1,000 entries of the leader.Promote it with a joint configuration change (see [[Membership changes with joint consensus]]).Remove the failed node.Leader keeps changingCheck for long pauses first: garbage collection, swap, or a noisy neighbour. The election timeout is 150 to 300 ms, so any pause longer than that triggers an election. See [[Postmortem INC-2317 election storm]].SELECT node_id, term, role, last_heartbeat_at
FROM raft_status
ORDER BY term DESC, node_id
LIMIT 20;Overview: [[Raft overview]].

A future is cancelled by dropping it, at any await point. `tokio::select!` drops every branch that did not win, which is where most cancellation bugs come from.Reads from `mpsc::Receiver::recv` are cancellation safe`tokio::time::sleep` is cancellation safeAudit every `select!` in the sync service for half-written stateReplace `read_exact` inside `select!` with a buffered framed readerAdd a test that cancels each handler at every await pointIf a function writes state, then awaits, then writes more state, cancellation can leave the first write without the second.Part of [[Rust async mental model]]. Review notes in [[Async Rust review notes]].

Ordered by risk.A `std::sync::Mutex` guard was held across an await in the presence handler; replaced with `tokio::sync::Mutex`.Two `select!` loops lost a partially read frame on cancellation; see [[Cancellation safety checklist]].Snapshot compression ran on a worker thread and stalled heartbeats for up to 80 ms; moved to `spawn_blocking`.An unbounded channel fed the indexer; bounded at 1,024 (see [[Backpressure with bounded channels]]).None of these showed up in unit tests. A log-structured merge tree turns random writes into sequential ones. Writes go to a write-ahead log and an in-memory memtable; full memtables are flushed as sorted, immutable SSTables; background compaction merges SSTables into larger ones level by level.Read pathCheck the memtable.Check L0 files, newest first (they can overlap).For each deeper level, binary search the one file whose key range covers the key, skipping it if its bloom filter says no.Write pathAppend to the WAL and fsync (or group commit).Insert into the memtable.When the memtable reaches 64 MiB, freeze it and flush it to L0.Deeper notes: [[Compaction strategies]], [[Bloom filter sizing]], [[SSTable format v2]], [[WAL recovery]], [[Block cache sizing]].

Compaction decides the engine's three amplification factors: write, read and space. You can make any two small; not all three.| Strategy | Write amplification | Read amplification | Space amplification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Leveled | high (10 to 30) | low | low (about 1.1) |
| Tiered | low | high | high (up to 2) |
| Hybrid (tiered L0, leveled below) | medium | medium | medium |We run leveled compaction with a size ratio of 10 and seven levels. L0 compaction triggers at 4 files; writes slow at 20 files and stop at 36.Spinning-disk deployments need different numbers; that work is tracked in [[Compaction tuning for HDD]]. What happens when compaction cannot keep up is in [[Write stall investigation]]. Back to [[LSM tree overview]].

A bloom filter answers "definitely not present" or "maybe present". Each SSTable carries one, so a point read can skip files without touching them.SizingWith k hash functions and m bits per key, the false positive rate is about (1 - e^(-k/m))^k. We use 10 bits per key with 7 hash functions, which gives roughly a 1 percent false positive rate. Going to 16 bits per key drops it to about 0.05 percent for 60 percent more filter memory.import math

def false_positive_rate(bits_per_key: float, hashes: int) -> float:
    return (1 - math.exp(-hashes / bits_per_key)) ** hashes

print(round(false_positive_rate(10, 7), 4))  # 0.0082Filters for the last level are skipped: most reads that reach it find the key. Back to [[LSM tree overview]].

Version 2 of our SSTable layout. All integers are little-endian unless marked varint.| Section | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Data blocks | 16 KiB target, prefix-compressed keys, restart point every 16 keys |
| Filter block | one bloom filter for the whole file |
| Index block | last key of each data block and its offset |
| Footer | offsets of filter and index, format version, CRC32C of the footer |Changes from v1:zstd compression per block instead of snappyCRC32C per block instead of per file, so a torn write is detected at the block that holds itThe footer moved to a fixed 64 bytes so readers find it with one seektype Footer struct {
	FilterOffset uint64
	FilterSize   uint64
	IndexOffset  uint64
	IndexSize    uint64
	Version      uint32
	Checksum     uint32
}Raft snapshots reuse this format ([[Raft log compaction and snapshots]]). Back to [[LSM tree overview]].

On startup the engine replays the write-ahead log into a fresh memtable. Records are framed with a length and a CRC32C, so a record torn by a crash is detected and recovery stops at the last complete record.Open the newest WAL segment named in the manifest.Read records until the end, or until a CRC mismatch.A mismatch in the last 32 KiB is a torn tail: truncate and continue.A mismatch anywhere else is corruption: refuse to start and page.Group commit batches fsync calls: one fsync covers every write that arrived during the previous one, which raised write throughput 4x with no loss of durability.Back to [[LSM tree overview]].

The block cache holds uncompressed data blocks. It is sized per node, not per table.Current size is 512 MiB per node, with a steady hit rate of 94 percent.Doubling it to 1 GiB raised the hit rate to 96 percent: not worth the memory.Index and filter blocks are pinned in the cache so a miss never costs two reads.| Cache size | Hit rate | p99 read latency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 256 MiB | 88% | 9.1 ms |
| 512 MiB | 94% | 4.2 ms |
| 1 GiB | 96% | 3.8 ms |Eviction is LRU with a small admission window; a scan does not flush hot blocks. Back to [[LSM tree overview]].

Semantic search embeds every block and finds the blocks whose vectors are closest to the query's. Exact search compares the query with every vector; approximate indexes trade a little recall for much less work.PiecesEmbedding model and normalisation: [[Embedding model choice]]Graph index: [[HNSW parameters]]Inverted file and compression: [[IVF and product quantization]]Measuring what we lose: [[Recall evaluation harness]]Combining with keyword search: [[Hybrid retrieval with BM25]]Every approximate result is filtered by permission before it is returned, and the filter runs before truncating to k, not after; otherwise a user with access to few notes gets fewer than k results.Recall without a baseline is a number without a meaning. Always report it against a brute-force scan.

Results of the October parameter sweep on the 1M-vector benchmark set (768 dimensions, cosine).| M | ef_construction | ef_search | Recall@10 | p99 latency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 100 | 64 | 0.912 | 1.1 ms |
| 16 | 200 | 128 | 0.948 | 1.9 ms |
| 32 | 200 | 128 | 0.973 | 2.4 ms |
| 48 | 400 | 256 | 0.986 | 5.2 ms |We settled on M = 32, ef_construction = 200 and ef_search = 128, for a recall@10 of 0.973 at 2.4 ms p99. Memory is about 1.4 times the raw vectors.import hnswlib

index = hnswlib.Index(space="cosine", dim=768)
index.init_index(max_elements=1_000_000, M=32, ef_construction=200)
index.set_ef(128)Back to [[Vector search overview]].

An inverted file index clusters vectors with k-means and searches only the nprobe closest clusters. Product quantization compresses each vector into a few bytes by quantizing sub-vectors separately.nlist = 4,096 clusters for 1M vectors (about 4 times the square root of n)nprobe = 32 gives recall@10 of 0.91 without re-rankingPQ with 64 sub-quantizers of 8 bits: 64 bytes per vector instead of 3 KiBRe-ranking the top 200 PQ candidates with exact distances brings recall@10 back to 0.97.Compared with [[HNSW parameters]], IVF-PQ uses a twentieth of the memory and is about three times slower at the same recall. Back to [[Vector search overview]].

Every index change is measured against an exact scan on the same queries.Sample 1,000 queries from real search logs (titles only, no note text).Compute the exact top 10 with a brute-force scan.Run the candidate index and compute recall@10 per query.Report the mean and the 5th percentile, because a good mean can hide queries with zero recall.def recall_at_k(exact: list[set[str]], approx: list[list[str]], k: int = 10) -> float:
    hits = [len(e & set(a[:k])) / k for e, a in zip(exact, approx)]
    return sum(hits) / len(hits)Back to [[Vector search overview]].

Keyword search wins on exact identifiers and rare words; semantic search wins on paraphrases. We run both and merge with reciprocal rank fusion with k = 60, which needs no score calibration.| Query type | BM25 nDCG@10 | Semantic nDCG@10 | Fused nDCG@10 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Identifiers (function names) | 0.81 | 0.42 | 0.80 |
| Natural language questions | 0.48 | 0.71 | 0.74 |The discovery panel shows the three signals separately and never blends them into one score, so a user can see why something was suggested. Back to [[Vector search overview]].

We compared three open embedding models on our own notes, labelled by two people for 300 query and note pairs.| Model | Dimensions | nDCG@10 | Throughput on CPU |

| small-en | 384 | 0.68 | 950 blocks/s |

| large-en | 1024 | 0.76 | 90 blocks/s |We chose base-multilingual: nearly the best quality, and it handles the Hindi, Japanese and German notes that the English models score poorly on.Vectors are normalised to unit length at write time, so cosine similarity is a dot product. Severity 2. Date 2026-08-19. Duration 47 minutes of degraded writes, 11 minutes of no writes. Blameless.SummaryA backfill job tripled write volume. Compaction could not keep up, the L0 file count reached 36, and the storage engine stopped accepting writes until compaction caught up.Root causeThe engine ran with max_background_compactions = 2, sized for normal load. With the backfill, L0 grew faster than two threads could merge it, and the write stall threshold of 36 L0 files was reached.MitigationRaised max_background_compactions from 2 to 6 at 14:38 UTC. Writes resumed at 14:49 UTC.Action itemsAlert when L0 exceeds 20 filesKeep 6 compaction threads permanentlyRate-limit backfills to 50 MB/sLoad test with 3x write volume before each releaseWorking notes: [[Write stall investigation]]. Strategy: [[Compaction strategies]].

Severity 2. Date 2026-09-26. Duration 23 minutes. Blameless.SummaryThe metadata cluster changed leader 41 times in 10 minutes. Writes that needed the metadata cluster failed or retried for the duration.Root causeA memory leak in the metrics exporter caused full garbage collection pauses of up to 1.2 seconds on two nodes. Each pause was longer than the 150 to 300 ms election timeout, so followers called elections, the paused node came back with a stale term, and the cycle repeated.FixesFixed the leak and capped exporter memoryAlert on GC pauses over 100 msAdd pre-vote so a returning node cannot disrupt a healthy leaderChaos scenario: pause a node for 2 s ([[Raft chaos test plan]])See [[Raft leader election timeouts]] for the timeout settings.
